units.source_text: 办完丧事的当天晚上，阿住和广次一起睡在设有佛坛的里屋一角的蚊帐内。

en.t: On the night after the funeral was over, Azumi and Hiroji slept together inside the mosquito net in a corner of the back room where the Buddhist altar stood.

units.source_text: 以往两人夜晚睡觉的时候屋里都是漆黑的，

en.t: Until then, whenever the two of them went to sleep at night, the room had always been pitch-dark,

units.source_text: 今晚佛坛上点着灯，再加上消毒水的味道混合陈旧的榻榻米所形成的奇怪气味，可能就是这个原因吧！

en.t: but tonight a lamp was lit on the altar, and perhaps it was because of the strange smell made by disinfectant mingling with the odor of old tatami.

units.source_text: 阿住躺在榻榻米上辗转发侧，难以入眠。

en.t: Azumi lay on the tatami, tossing from side to side, unable to fall asleep.

units.source_text: 阿民的死确实给她带来了巨大的幸福感。

en.t: Atami's death had indeed brought her an immense feeling of happiness.

units.source_text: 从现在开始，她再也不用像从前那样操劳了，也不用担心村民的闲言碎语。

en.t: From now on, she would no longer have to toil as she had before, nor would she have to worry about the villagers' gossip.

units.source_text: 家里约莫有三千圆的存款，还有几亩田地。

en.t: The household had about three thousand yen in savings, as well as several mu of farmland.

units.source_text: 从此之后，她就可以和孙子一起吃大米饭，随时带着草袋去买自己喜欢吃的咸鳟鱼。

en.t: After this, she could eat white rice with her grandson and, whenever she liked, take a straw bag and go buy the salted trout she loved.

units.source_text: 阿住实在记不起来自己的一生之中，有什么时候曾像现在一般轻松自在过？

en.t: Azumi simply could not remember any time in her life when she had ever felt as light and free as she did now.

units.source_text: 像现在一般轻松自在过？

en.t: Had she ever felt as light and free as she did now?

units.source_text: ——九年前某一夜的记忆突然就清晰的出现在她脑海里。

en.t: A memory of a certain night nine years earlier suddenly appeared clearly in her mind.

units.source_text: 那一晚如释重负的感觉，和今夜差不多。

en.t: The sense of relief she had felt that night was much the same as tonight.

units.source_text: 那是她的亲生儿子葬礼介绍的夜晚。

en.t: It was the night after the funeral of her own son had ended.

units.source_text: ——是生了唯一孙子的儿媳妇的葬礼结束的夜晚。

en.t: It was the night after the funeral of the daughter-in-law who had borne her only grandson.
